findings.practical_consequence: Without a planner-defined authoritative producer and correlated safe event for each supported dispatch surface, non-argv model actions remain invisible and cannot participate in matching, learning, correction, or acceptance; unsupported proprietary host classes must instead surface an explicit unsupported result.
evidence: Required side: E-REQ, requirements.json:146-188 requires every action class to have a producer, durable record, observer consumer, enforcement point, or confirmed visible absence.

Current side: E-WORKMEM at scripts/work_memory.py:49 and scripts/work_memory.py:1615-1669 represents checked execution claims and returns; E-CHECKEXEC at scripts/sequence_checked_exec.py:93-104 produces those records only for direct argv.

Missing-class side: E-EXECUTOR at mcp-agents-workflow/src/workflow_orch/agents/executor.py:382-549 and E-CLI-BASE at mcp-agents-workflow/src/workflow_orch/cli/base.py:51-78 expose aggregate phase/CLI results rather than canonical per-action events; E-MAWF-TOOLS at tool_translator.py:56-100 confirms file, shell, web, and MCP capabilities can occur behind that aggregate boundary.
findings.evidence_limitation: The frozen roots expose no supported proprietary Codex desktop hook or schema; the planner must use the named host-owner fixture route and keep unavailable classes fail-visible rather than infer them from transcripts or final responses.

findings.practical_consequence: A model can currently improvise before entering the governed sequence path; the planner must place deterministic applicability and activation before effect dispatch while preserving existing execution approvals and failing visibly on ambiguity, staleness, or unsupported actions.
evidence: Required side: E-REQ, requirements.json:194-211 requires a compatible gold sequence to be selected before dispatch and improvisation to be rejected or explicitly governed.

Current consumer side: E-WORKMEM at scripts/work_memory.py:1314 begins selection only after cmd_select is invoked, and E-GUARD at scripts/sequence_guard.py:679 begins enforcement only after cmd_guard is invoked.
Advisory side: E-SKILL-DEPLOYED at /Users/kamenkamenov/.codex/skills/sequence-runner/SKILL.md:13-18 instructs the model to select, activate, and guard but supplies no host-wide interceptor.
findings.evidence_limitation: No accessible Codex-host source proves arbitrary desktop pre-dispatch interception; the candidate names a finite host-owner fixture route and a fail-visible unsupported outcome.

findings.practical_consequence: A successful unrecorded operation does not yet traverse capture, qualification, promotion, registered verification, and later pre-dispatch reuse as one closed system; the planner must connect those existing gates without reconstructing or guessing missing steps.
evidence: Required side: E-REQ, requirements.json:217-234 and requirements.json:471-489 requires one deduplicated, complete proven path to become silver, then gold, then be reused before dispatch.

Producer side: E-OBSERVER at scripts/sequence_observer.py:130-220 reconstructs only complete checked-exec success evidence and E-BOOTSTRAP at scripts/discovery_bootstrap.py:250 creates a supplied complete discovery.

Downstream side: E-LIFECYCLE at scripts/discovery_promotion_lifecycle.py:266-345 and E-PROMOTE at scripts/sequence_promote.py:222-319 expose qualification, promotion, and registered verification as explicitly invoked controller stages; E-E2E confirms the lifecycle works when explicitly driven rather than autonomously closed.

findings.practical_consequence: A model’s statement that its action caused an issue cannot currently prevent recurrence because it is not authoritatively joined to the dispatched action, failure, blocker occurrence, replacement, and same-path successor proof; the planner must define that causal join and produce a corrected or held reusable path.
evidence: Required side: E-REQ, requirements.json:240-280 requires self-diagnosis to remain a signal until action, failure, blocker, replacement, and successor evidence prove the correction and exclude the wrong step.
Current lifecycle side: E-WORKMEM at scripts/work_memory.py:63-89 and scripts/work_memory.py:1795-1961 durably represents corrections, bundle transitions, and successor verification.

Missing-join side: E-BLOCKER records governed blocker fingerprints and occurrences but has no model-statement/action correlation contract; E-EXECUTOR at executor.py:491-549 exposes aggregate execution metadata rather than an authoritative internal action/failure stream.

findings.practical_consequence: Correcting a registered sequence in place cannot guarantee that the defective version remains auditable yet non-selectable or that readers cut over atomically to a verified replacement; the planner must define immutable version identity, quarantine, requalification, registered verification, and selector cutover.
evidence: Required side: E-REQ, requirements.json:286-304 requires the old version to remain auditable and non-selectable while only a gated replacement becomes selectable.

Current mutation side: E-WORKMEM correction and bundle-transition events at scripts/work_memory.py:63-76 and scripts/work_memory.py:1795-1961 preserve correction evidence but retain the same subject lineage.

Registration side: E-PROMOTE at scripts/sequence_promote.py:222-319 creates a registered identity and rejects an already-registered sequence ID; E-LIFECYCLE at scripts/discovery_promotion_lifecycle.py:498-541 corrects an existing registered subject without an immutable replacement-version selector contract; E-RECON explicitly lacks versioned recognition/repair rules.

findings.practical_consequence: Without machine-readable silver/gold transitions and stable opportunity-based metric definitions, growth can be reported without proving more complete captures, verified reuse, corrected reuse, or reduced wrong-step recurrence; the planner must encode the lifecycle states, transition evidence, numerators, denominators, and identity joins.
evidence: Required side: E-REQ, requirements.json:310-349 requires canonical silver/gold states plus eligible-observation, transition, reuse, correction, false-match, hold, duplicate, and recurrence metrics.

Current lifecycle side: E-DISCOVERY at scripts/sequence_discovery_log.py:395-447 exposes discovery, ready, and overdue states, while E-REGISTRY defines registered catalog entries without silver/gold fields.

Current measurement side: E-WORKMEM at scripts/work_memory.py:2053-2144 computes run and correction-effect metrics but does not provide eligible-opportunity, silver conversion, gold reuse, false-match, evidence-hold, or known-wrong-step-recurrence denominators.

findings.practical_consequence: Independent ledger, workflow-state, discovery, and registry writers can otherwise resume or merge with duplicate candidates, lost corrections, stale selection, or branch-local evidence; the planner must choose one canonical owner and define idempotent event union, conflict resolution, current-version synchronization, and feedback rule-version consumption.
evidence: Required side: E-REQ, requirements.json:378-396 and requirements.json:448-465 requires interruption-safe cross-runtime ownership and immutable identity-bound feedback semantics.

Ledger side: E-WORKMEM at scripts/work_memory.py:831-855 provides event-ID conflict detection and scripts/work_memory.py:2161-2195 merges ledgers atomically, but it does not define cross-store current-version ownership.

Sibling-store side: E-WORKFLOW-STATE atomically persists separate per-run workflow/phase JSON without sequence candidate/version merge semantics; E-RECON at discovery_candidate_reconciliation.py:431-466 and discovery_candidate_reconciliation.py:671-689 reconciles candidate snapshots but does not synchronize a canonical version across runtimes and branches.
